title: The Fourier entropy–influence conjecture
decision_reason: Exact canonical Boolean formulation, independent current corroboration, full relevant resolution-scope comparisons, duplicate review, separated A65 self-review and technical checks passed. One unintegrated family; no permanent ID.

problem_fingerprint.objects: Every integer n>=1 and every function f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, with the uniform probability measure on the cube. No monotonicity, balance, bounded degree, formula size or symmetry assumption.
problem_fingerprint.fourier_normalization: For every S subset of [n], chi_S(x)=product_(i in S) x_i, with chi_empty=1, and fhat(S)=2^(-n) sum_x f(x) chi_S(x). Parseval gives sum_S fhat(S)^2=1.
problem_fingerprint.entropy: H(f)=sum_(S subset of [n]) fhat(S)^2 log_2(1/fhat(S)^2), including the empty set and defining a zero summand to be zero.
problem_fingerprint.influence: For uniform X, X^(i) flips its ith bit. Inf_i(f)=Pr[f(X)!=f(X^(i))]=sum_(S containing i) fhat(S)^2. I(f)=sum_i Inf_i(f)=sum_S |S| fhat(S)^2.
problem_fingerprint.target: There is one finite universal constant C>0 such that H(f)<=C I(f) for every n and every Boolean-valued f.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: C is independent of dimension and function. The assertion is a nonasymptotic inequality, not a claim about most functions, bounded-complexity subclasses or a fixed proposed sharp numerical constant.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Shannon entropy of the squared Fourier coefficient distribution, not entropy of f(X), Fourier min-entropy, biased-input entropy, or matrix/quantum entropy. Boolean output is essential; no general real-valued extension is asserted.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One canonical entry; equivalent average-sensitivity wording, logarithm bases, spectral concentration consequences and restricted classes receive no separate count.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Symmetric, fixed-part symmetric and globally read-once decision-tree classes.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The restrictions do not cover arbitrary Boolean functions; the part-dependent constant is not uniform as the number of parts grows.
The coordinate entropy sum need not be O(I(f)); it still contains small-influence logarithmic costs.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: H(f) <= c1 I(f)+c2 sum_i Inf_i(f) log(1/Inf_i(f)).
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The extra coordinate term is not uniformly bounded by I. The 2025 note acknowledges related KMS11 work; it does not announce a resolution.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Min-entropy and spectral concentration with I/Var and logarithmic dependence; truncated Shannon entropy with |S| log(|S|+1) weights.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Neither large-coefficient existence nor fixed-tail concentration proves the proposed full Shannon-entropy inequality.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: FEI in exponentially small-influence and linearly large-entropy regimes; constants depend on the regime or Fourier l1 norm. Sublinear extensions would imply full FEI.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The extensions are conditional implications, not proved unrestricted inequalities.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Read-k decision-tree FEI constant O(sqrt(k)), with at most k occurrences of each variable across the whole tree.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: A growing k leaves a growing constant; per-path read-once would incorrectly include all Boolean functions.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A monotone family violates a stronger auxiliary splitting inequality for the designated variable but satisfies FEI by another split.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Failure of this induction route does not refute the target inequality.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Semi-separated stopping trees and separated tribe families satisfy FEI; stopping functions must already satisfy FEI.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The separated-variable and stopping hypotheses are proper restrictions, not an all-function theorem.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Unit-modulus complex functions lift to Hermitian involutions by a block dilation.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Complex output is not scalar {-1,1}; the extra matrix coordinate does not supply a Boolean counterexample.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Quantum examples have influence below 2 and Pauli entropy growing like log n.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Quantum Pauli weights differ from classical parity weights. Global diagonalization does not preserve the coordinate influence structure.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Homogeneous degree-d quantum Boolean operators have entropy Theta(d^2) and influence d.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The model permits noncommuting Pauli directions. Only Z-supported diagonal operators recover the classical class, and no such classical construction is claimed.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Strict-avalanche, plateaued and monomial classes; concatenation assumes already-admissible functions with disjoint Fourier support.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Asymptotic log-density one is not all functions. Unrestricted Shannon decompositions do not satisfy the disjoint-support hypothesis.

independent_corroboration.qualification: Separate author groups explicitly retain the classical conjecture in June and August 2026. S26 overlaps SVZ26; LH25 is withdrawn. Versions, mirrors and the related KMS/Han coordinate-entropy estimates are not counted as extra independent works.

normalization_checks: Uniform measure; real scalar {-1,1} outputs; every dimension and every function. Parseval gives a probability measure without additional normalization.
All Fourier subsets, including the empty set, appear. A zero coefficient contributes zero; constants have H=I=0, so the target is non-strict.
SVZ26 omits the empty coefficient in one classical display. For a=fhat(empty)^2, a log_2(1/a) <= (1-a)/ln 2 <= I/ln 2, so existence of a universal constant is equivalent.
Only one finite universal C is requested. Finite lower bounds on the best C and examples defeating a chosen small C do not disprove FEI.
Spectral Shannon entropy is distinct from output entropy, min-entropy, relative/biased entropy and quantum operator entropy.

Under FEI, retaining coefficients of squared magnitude at least 2^(-C I/epsilon) gives at most 2^(C I/epsilon) terms and omitted squared mass at most epsilon. Constants are handled separately. This is a representation statement, not an algorithm.
The stated DNF consequence allows membership queries and fixes accuracy. It does not solve entry 329's passive learning model; the stronger Mansour exponent O(log(1/epsilon)) is not asserted.
Read-k counts variable occurrences over the entire tree. Restricted subclasses and equivalent formulations remain one candidate family.
